utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. If there are no procedural issues to be dealt with, then we move into closed session. And could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we adjourn, I'd like to read one decision by the Chamber. The Chamber now delivers its oral decision on the Prosecution's motion for the admission of evidence of witness Miroslav Deronjic pursuant to Rule 92 quater, for which written reasons will follow in due course. On the 18th of June, 2007, the Prosecution filed its motion for the admission of evidence of witness Miroslav Deronjic pursuant to Rule 92 quater. On the 22nd of June, 2007, the Prosecution filed an addendum to the motion containing the death certificate of the witness. On the 7th of October, 2009, the Prosecution filed a corrigendum to the motion, correcting discrepancies between the body of the motion and the annexes thereto by withdrawing its request for admission of the testimony of Deronjic in the Blagojevic and Jokic case and the Krstic case, while at the same time adding a request for the admission of additional transcripts of the Deronjic testimony in the Krajisnik case. The Trial Chamber grants the Prosecution's motion including its addendum and corrigendum. As a result, the Chamber admits the testimony of Deronjic in the Milosevic case dated the 26th and 27th of November, 2003, and his testimony in the Krajisnik case dated 12, 13th, 16th, 18th, and 19th of February, 2004. It further admits Deronjic's witness statement dated the 25th of November 2003 publicly. The Chamber also admitted all associated exhibits publicly, with the exception of P1311 and P1328 since they have already been admitted into evidence. Finally, the Chamber admits the death certificate of Miroslav Deronjic under seal. Although the Trial Chamber is inclined to admit the aforementioned testimony of Deronjic in the Milosevic case and the Krajisnik case publicly, on the 5th of July, 2010, the Prosecution requested the, and I quote "redaction of information given in closed session" referring to the information given by Deronjic. The Prosecution is requested to identify any such closed session portions of Deronjic's testimony during the next week's housekeeping session. As I stated earlier, the Chamber will provide written reasons for its decision in due course, and this concludes the Chamber's decision. We adjourn for the day and we'll resume Monday, the 17th of December -- no, now I'm making a mistake. One second, please. We resume on Monday, the 13th of December at quarter past 2.00 in this same Courtroom II. If I said November, I'm saved by others because it is of course the 13th of December. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can the accused be absent Monday, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on housekeeping sessions, the Chamber as a rule accepts if the accused choose not to be present. Of course, they are fully entitled to be present, but if they do not appear, the Chamber will accept that on even without knowing the reasons. That being on the record we stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 13th day of December, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.15 p.m.
